gloss: buying up; hoarding; cornering the supply

definitions.gloss: buying up; panic hoarding; cornering the supply
definitions.explanation: Buying all or most of an available stock, either by consumers stripping the shelves in a shortage or by a buyer cornering a market for profit. The noun form of {買|か}い{占|し}める.

examples.japanese: マスクの{買|か}い{占|し}めが{起|お}きた。
examples.english: Panic buying of masks broke out.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{占|し}めはご{遠慮|えんりょ}くださいと{張|は}り{紙|がみ}があった。
examples.english: There was a notice asking customers to refrain from bulk-buying.

examples.japanese: {品薄|しなうす}の{報道|ほうどう}が{買|か}い{占|し}めを{招|まね}き、かえって{品不足|しなぶそく}がひどくなった。
examples.english: Reports of short supply triggered hoarding, which only made the shortage worse.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {買|か}い{占|し}めが{起|お}きる: for hoarding to break out
- {買|か}い{占|し}めを{防|ふせ}ぐ: to prevent hoarding
- {土地|とち}の{買|か}い{占|し}め: buying up land
- {転売|てんばい}{目的|もくてき}の{買|か}い{占|し}め: buying up for resale

USAGE:
The word carries clear disapproval: the buyer is taking more than their share or manipulating supply. Ordinary bulk shopping is {まとめ{買|が}い}, which is neutral and even thrifty.
